chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) is treated with 1. NH3, HCN; 2. Aqueous H3O+ / heat?
questions.explanation: Treating Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) with 1. NH3, HCN; 2. Aqueous H3O+ / heat yields (±)-Alanine (2-aminopropanoic acid). Rationale: Condensation of aldehyde with ammonia and cyanide yields alpha-aminonitrile, hydrolyzed in acid to amino acid.

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Propanoic acid into (±)-Alanine?
questions.explanation: To convert Propanoic acid into (±)-Alanine, the appropriate reagent is 1. Br2, PBr3; 2. Excess NH3 (aq). Rationale: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky alpha-bromination followed by nucleophilic substitution with excess ammonia.

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Diethyl acetamidomalonate is treated with 1. NaOEt; 2. Benzyl chloride; 3. Aqueous H3O+, heat?
questions.explanation: Treating Diethyl acetamidomalonate with 1. NaOEt; 2. Benzyl chloride; 3. Aqueous H3O+, heat yields Phenylalanine. Rationale: Alkylation of enolate followed by acid-catalyzed ester hydrolysis, amide cleavage, and thermal decarboxylation.

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Alanine into Ruhemann's purple dye + Acetaldehyde + CO2?

options.label: C
options.text: 1. NaOEt; 2. Benzyl chloride; 3. Aqueous H3O+, heat

questions.explanation: To convert Alanine into Ruhemann's purple dye + Acetaldehyde + CO2, the appropriate reagent is Ninhydrin reagent / heat. Rationale: Oxidative decarboxylation and deamination of alpha-amino acid condenses with ninhydrin to form deep purple dye.

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Alanyl-glycyl-valine (Ala-Gly-Val) is treated with 1. Phenyl isothiocyanate (PITC) / base; 2. CF3COOH?
questions.explanation: Treating Alanyl-glycyl-valine (Ala-Gly-Val) with 1. Phenyl isothiocyanate (PITC) / base; 2. CF3COOH yields PTH-Alanine + Glycyl-valine (Gly-Val). Rationale: PITC selectively labels and cleaves the N-terminal amino acid as a phenylthiohydantoin (PTH) derivative.

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Alanine into N-tert-Butoxycarbonylalanine (N-Boc-Alanine)?
questions.explanation: To convert Alanine into N-tert-Butoxycarbonylalanine (N-Boc-Alanine), the appropriate reagent is Di-tert-butyl dicarbonate (Boc2O) / aqueous NaOH. Rationale: Boc anhydride acylates the amino group, protecting it against unwanted nucleophilic attacks.

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Trifluoroacetic acid (CF3COOH) in CH2Cl2 to yield Alanine (trifluoroacetate salt) + Isobutylene + CO2 as the major product?
questions.explanation: N-Boc-Alanine reacts with Trifluoroacetic acid (CF3COOH) in CH2Cl2 to yield Alanine (trifluoroacetate salt) + Isobutylene + CO2. Rationale: Acid-catalyzed cleavage of tert-butyl carbamate releases isobutylene gas and carbon dioxide.

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Alanine is treated with 9-Fluorenylmethyl chloroformate (Fmoc-Cl) / base?
questions.explanation: Treating Alanine with 9-Fluorenylmethyl chloroformate (Fmoc-Cl) / base yields N-Fmoc-Alanine. Rationale: Fmoc-Cl masks the amino group as a base-labile fluorenyl carbamate protecting group.

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: Which starting material will react with 20% Piperidine in DMF to yield Alanine + Dibenzofulvene-piperidine adduct as the major product?
questions.explanation: N-Fmoc-Alanine reacts with 20% Piperidine in DMF to yield Alanine + Dibenzofulvene-piperidine adduct. Rationale: Secondary amine piperidine abstracts acidic fluorenyl proton, triggering E1cB elimination of protecting group.

questions.chapter_title: Biomolecules: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Resin-bound Glycine + N-Boc-Alanine is treated with DCC (dicyclohexylcarbodiimide)?
questions.explanation: Treating Resin-bound Glycine + N-Boc-Alanine with DCC (dicyclohexylcarbodiimide) yields Resin-bound N-Boc-Alanylglycine + DCU. Rationale: DCC activates the carboxylic acid to form a peptide bond while the growing chain is anchored to polystyrene beads.
